intent: log line starting with a given level
description: A log line is valid if it begins with one of the severity levels INFO, WARN, ERROR, or DEBUG in uppercase. The level must be immediately followed by a colon and a single space. The rest of the line may contain any characters except line breaks. The whole line must be at least the level, colon, and space long, and empty messages are allowed after the prefix.

intent: line containing a stack trace frame
description: A line is a stack trace frame if it starts with optional spaces, then the word 'at', followed by a single space, then a module or file path containing at least one slash-separated component, optionally followed by a colon and a line number, and optionally followed by a colon and a column number. Only the frame format is checked. The path components may contain letters, digits, underscores, hyphens, dots, and slashes, but no spaces. The entire line must consist only of this frame.

intent: string that does not start with a prefix
description: Accept any string that does not start with the prefix "tmp_". The string can be empty.

intent: number not ending in a given digit
description: A whole number (digits only, at least one) that does not end with the digit 0.

intent: word that is not one of a list of reserved words
description:
A variable name in our config language must match all of these constraints:
1. It is a non-empty sequence of ASCII letters, digits and underscores, and it may not start with a digit.
2. It must not be exactly one of the reserved words (case-sensitive): if, else, then, end, do, while, for, return, break, continue, true, false, null.
No whitespace or other characters are allowed.

unix absolute path: starts with slash, one or more path segments separated by slashes, last segment may be empty (trailing slash allowed), each segment is one or more characters except slash and newline
hidden dotfile name: starts with a dot, followed by one or more characters that are not slash, backslash, or newline; the name after the dot cannot be another dot

intent: git branch name following a convention
